q: Bartolo Mascarello's famous label and its slogan:
ans: 'No barrique, no Berlusconi' — the hand-drawn manifesto label
exp: Maria Teresa continues the single-blend Barolo; the label is the philosophy.

q: Which vintage made Screaming Eagle's reputation, and which made Harlan's?
ans: Screaming Eagle's 1992 debut; Harlan's 1990 first release (held back, released 1996) and 1994 breakthrough
exp: Napa's cult era dates precisely from these bottlings.

q: Who was Jules Chauvet and why does he matter?
accept: chemist beaujolais natural wine theorist no sulfur
ans: A Beaujolais négociant and research chemist whose work on native yeasts and minimal sulfur inspired Lapierre's generation — the natural movement's intellectual father
exp: He was also a formidable taster and aroma scientist.

q: Name the four 'Gang of Four' Beaujolais producers.
accept: lapierre foillard thevenet breton guy breton jean-paul thevenet
ans: Marcel Lapierre, Jean Foillard, Guy Breton, Jean-Paul Thévenet
exp: Kermit Lynch's name for them; Morgon is their heartland.

q: Name three producers who define a region so completely that their style is mistaken for the appellation's.
accept: guigal cote rotie quintarelli amarone lopez de heredia rioja penfolds
ans: Guigal in Côte-Rôtie, Quintarelli in Amarone, López de Heredia in Rioja, Penfolds in Australian Shiraz — each so dominant the house style reads as regional typicity
exp: Beware: your reference bottle may be an outlier, not a template.

q: Recite Hermitage's principal climats west to east.
accept: bessards meal ermite murets greffieux diognieres
ans: West to east: Les Bessards with L'Ermite on the summit above it; the central pair of Le Méal (upper) and Les Greffieux (on the slope below); then Péléat and Les Rocoules; then Les Murets and Les Diognières on gentler clay
exp: Granite west (Bessards) to loess-limestone east — structure to perfume.

q: Chave's rare sweet Hermitage and Guigal's rare sweet Condrieu are respectively:
accept: vin de paille and luminescence doux
ans: Vin de Paille (Chave); late-harvest Condrieu (e.g., Guigal 'Luminescence', Cuilleron 'Ayguets')
exp: Sweet Condrieu was the historical norm — dry is the modern reinvention.

q: Which Côte-Rôtie lieu-dit does Jamet's village blend famously span, and what defines the domaine's method?
ans: Jamet blends ~25 lieux-dits across the slope, largely whole-cluster — the anti-single-vineyard argument
exp: Guigal's La-Las vs Jamet's assemblage is the appellation's philosophical axis.

q: Explain 'plan de Dieu' and its climate logic.
accept: cotes du rhone villages plateau mistral
ans: A Côtes du Rhône Villages named geographical denomination — not a commune but a mistral-scoured alluvial plateau of galets ('God's plain') shared by Camaret-sur-Aigues, Jonquières, Travaillan and Violès, ripening muscular Grenache
exp: Master-level southern Rhône means knowing the named villages' characters.

accept: dries disease stresses vines shuts stomata
ans: It sanitizes (drying disease pressure) but also stresses vines to stomatal shutdown in drought years
exp: Roughly 100-150 days a year in the lower Rhône valley — 300 is the sunshine figure, not the wind; windbreak cypress rows are the tell.

exp: One of France's smallest AOPs and the smallest single-estate appellation outside Burgundy — though La Romanée, Criots-Bâtard-Montrachet, La Grande Rue and Romanée-Conti are all smaller.

q: Saint-Péray's two permitted grapes and its Wagner connection:
ans: Marsanne and Roussanne; Wagner ordered 100 bottles of Saint-Péray mousseux while composing Parsifal
exp: The oral's beloved anecdote category: composers and cuvées.

accept: all 13 varieties mourvedre heavy flash heating vinification
flash pasteurization must thirteen varieties organic since 1960s
ans: All thirteen varieties planted (Mourvèdre-heavy blend); brief thermo-treatment (flash-heating) of the harvest at reception; organic farming since 1950 and biodynamic since 1974 — among the earliest in France
exp: The 'flash' treatment is their oxidase answer — controversial, effective.

q: Rasteau's three AOP colors of fortified plus its dry promotion year:
accept: 2010 dry reds vdn ambre tuile grenat
ans: VDN in grenat/tuilé/ambré (rosé too) — and dry reds promoted to cru in 2010
The commune banned flying saucers ('cigares volants') from landing in the vineyards — still on the books
exp: Bonny Doon's Le Cigare Volant toasts it; orals end on charm sometimes.

q: Characterize 1961 and 1978 in the Northern Rhône.
ans: 1961: Jaboulet's La Chapelle — perhaps the century's most celebrated bottle; 1978: monumental, structured, the modern benchmark
exp: Both are cited whenever Hermitage's ageability is questioned.
